To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) our proposed approach is able to predict volatility in stock markets using textual information from annual reports; (2) the proposed approach significantly outperformed the state-of-the-art; (3) we investigated different fusion methods to incorporate market information and showed that a simple approach of averaging the predictions of the textual and market data models is the best; and (4) the proposed approach is able predict volatility for different sectors of the stock market.

(i) our approach significantly outperformed the state-ofthe-art, (ii) our approach is robust to the choice of the embedding model, (iii) our approach is more robust than the state-of-the-art, and (iv) the choice of the word embeddings model does not have a significant impact on the results
the word embedding-based IR methods outperform the state-of-the-art methods, and the fusion of text and market data is not beneficial.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the use of textual information can significantly contribute to the prediction of market volatility.
the use of IR term weighting models and their extension with related terms using word embedding techniques can improve the prediction of stock volatility.
the textual information from financial disclosures of companies in financial sectors can effectively be utilized to forecast the volatility of their stocks.

the textual analysis of financial reports is an effective tool for volatility prediction.
word embeddings can improve the performance of IR models in sentiment analysis.
the textual information of annual disclosures is a valuable resource for predicting market volatility, and that our word embedding-based IR models are promising for this task.
